newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse ends mixed, turnover down.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse ends mixed, turnover down.

text.p: Bucharest bourse share prices closed in a mixed picture on Monday amid weak buying interest from foreign investors, traders said.
"The bearish mood persisted as many stocks had been perceived as too expensive," a trader said.
"Foreign buyers stayed on the sideline, and probably they will not rush to buy throughout the week," another said.

Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, went down from the Friday session, sliding 2.2, 2.33 and 2.21 percent respectively.
"Some brokerage houses had advised their clients to take profits," a trader commented.
The closing prices of 21 stocks inched up, 19 went down and three were flat. Two stocks stayed suspended and another two had no trades.
Volume inched down to 2.25 million shares from 2.3 million last Friday, while turnover slipped to 9.14 billion lei from 10.6 billion previously.
First-tier listings took around 78 percent of overall turnover with chemical plant Oltchim and car parts manufacturer Compa COPA.BX the most active stocks.
Oltchim closed 100 lei firmer at 4,450 in late trading, while Compa inched down 50 lei to 2,850.
Fertiliser maker Azomures gained 50 lei to close at 3,800.

On the second tier interest was thin with most listings losing steam under selling pressure. Ciprom steel pipe maker, which dominated trading in this section last week, went down, shedding 250 lei to close at 1,350.
